data.author: sammycage
data.article_summary: PlutoFilter 是一个单头文件、零分配的图像滤镜库，用C语言编写。它可以快速应用可链式的图像效果，无需动态内存分配，兼容SVG和CSS滤镜语义，跨平台一致性强。该库为自包含形式，支持头文件模式和实现模式。使用时，可在单一源文件中定义 `PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION` 来包含实现代码。它提供了多种滤镜效果，如高斯模糊、颜色变换、灰度、饱和度、亮度、对比度、混合模式等。此外，还支持自定义颜色变换矩阵，适用于图像处理应用。

主要讨论点：PlutoFilter库的功能、实现细节及其在不同场景下的适用性

不同观点：
• jlundberg对该库的示例和整体实现表示赞赏，但尚未找到具体的使用场景，不过觉得可能已经有潜在需求。
• anitil关注库的"零分配"声明，指出尽管使用栈分配而不是动态分配，但仍有小规模的固定分配，提醒在嵌入式环境下需要注意栈空间。
• mnaimd称赞该库易于集成到现有项目中，并特别提到其使用C99编写，对开发者友好。
• dxroshan对项目表示祝贺，并表达了对相关项目（如PlutoVG、LunaSVG、PlutoSVG）的喜爱。
• kookamamie认可该库的功能，但指出其在处理ARGB输入时默认假设为premultiplied-alpha，这可能对某些用例不太适用，需要进行unpremultiply操作。
• ephou7质疑单头文件形式的优势，认为像GEGL这样更强大的库可能在功能上更有竞争力。
• rossant关注库的性能，询问是否支持SIMD或多核能力以提升计算效率。
• countfeng简单表达了对"Blend model"的喜爱，但没有深入讨论具体细节。

补充讨论：
• 关于库的性能和资源使用，anitil提到了栈空间分配问题，rossant则关注SIMD和多核支持，显示出对该库在嵌入式或高性能场景下表现的关注。

PlutoFilter
PlutoFilter is a single-header, zero-allocation image filter library written in C. It applies fast, chainable image effects without any dynamic memory allocation. Compatible with SVG and CSS filter semantics, it makes it easy to reproduce visual effects consistently across platforms.
Installation
PlutoFilter is a self-contained, single-header library written in standard C99. It can be used in two modes: header-only or implementation. In
header-only mode
, simply include the header in any source or header file. This exposes all API declarations but does not include the implementation.
To include the actual implementation, define
PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION
in
one
.c
or
.cpp
file before including the header:
#define
PLUTOFILTER_IMPLEMENTATION
#include
"plutofilter.h"
In all other source files, include the header as usual:
#include
"plutofilter.h"
The macro
PLUTOFILTER_API
controls the linkage of public functions. By default, it expands to
extern
, but if you define
PLUTOFILTER_BUILD_STATIC
before including the header, all functions will be declared
static
instead. This is useful when embedding the library in a single translation unit to avoid symbol collisions.

data.title: RisingWave: An Open‑Source Stream‑Processing and Management Platform
data.author: Sheldon_fun
data.article_summary:
RisingWave是一个流处理与管理平台，旨在以最简单且最具成本效益的方式处理、分析和管理实时事件数据，支持Apache Iceberg™开放表格式。它提供兼容PostgreSQL的SQL接口和DataFrame风格的Python接口，能够每秒处理数百万事件，进行实时流数据和历史数据的连接与分析，支持低延迟的即席查询，并将结果持久化到Apache Iceberg™或其他下游系统。

RisingWave的关键特性包括：
- 高吞吐量：每秒处理百万级事件。
- 实时处理：增量处理实时和历史数据。
- 低延迟查询：支持即席查询。
- 内置存储：支持Apache Iceberg™，实现低成本数据存储和开放访问。

其设计优势在于：
- PostgreSQL兼容性：支持熟悉的SQL语法。
- 无需手动调优：简化状态管理。
- 使用S3作为主要存储：提供高性能和快速恢复能力，支持动态扩展。
- 弹性磁盘缓存：优化性能并降低成本。

RisingWave适用于流式分析和事件驱动应用等场景，如股票交易、体育博彩和物联网监控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RisingWave及类似工具（如Materialize、ClickHouse）在实际应用中的价值和使用场景。

不同观点：
• **up2isomorphism** 认为当前已经有太多类似工具，对人们继续涌入这个领域表示不解，暗示市场可能已经饱和。
• **jsumrall** 对RisingWave和Materialize表示了初步的好感，尤其对RisingWave团队有正面印象。不过最终选择了ClickHouse，因为其物化视图功能易于设置且性能良好，相比之下Timescale虽然性能不错但需要更多专业知识。
• **synthc** 希望了解RisingWave在实际生产环境中的表现，表明目前缺乏相关经验报告。
• **rubenvanwyk** 对RisingWave的实际用例感到好奇，特别是除了实时分析和可观察性之外，是否还有人将其用于增量视图维护（如在Postgres中）。
• **vivzkestrel** 提出一个基础性问题，即在什么情况下应该选择RisingWave或Kafka这样的系统，而不是传统的Redis PubSub系统。
• **shepardrtc** 对RisingWave的架构图表示赞赏，并询问使用了什么工具来制作。
• **esafak** 对RisingWave作为基于Rust的Flink简化版表示疑问，质疑其是否真的更简单。
• **acjohnson55** 直接比较RisingWave和Materialize，希望了解两者之间的优劣。

补充讨论：
• 关于RisingWave的生产环境经验报告较少，用户对其实际表现存在疑问（synthc）。
• 用户对RisingWave的实际应用场景有不同看法，有人关注其在Postgres中增量视图维护的潜力（rubenvanwyk）。
• 基础性比较，如与传统Redis PubSub的对比，显示出对何时选择复杂系统与简单系统的困惑（vivzkestrel）。
• 架构图的制作工具引发关注，显示出对技术展示方式的兴趣（shepardrtc）。
• RisingWave与Materialize的直接对比显示出用户在选择类似工具时的困惑，尤其是简化程度和功能强弱的权衡（acjohnson55, esafak）。

争议焦点：
• RisingWave是否真的比其他工具（如Flink、Materialize）更简单易用，且能满足复杂需求。
• 在何种情况下应该选择RisingWave这样的系统，而不是使用传统的简单系统如Redis PubSub。

🌊 Ride the Wave of Streaming Data.
Docs

Benchmarks

RisingWave is a stream processing and management platform designed to offer the
simplest
and
most cost-effective
way to
process
,
analyze
, and
manage
real-time event data — with built-in support for the
Apache Iceberg™
open table format. It provides both a Postgres-compatible
SQL interface
and a DataFrame-style
Python interface
.
RisingWave can
ingest
millions of events per second, continuously
join and analyze
live streams with historical data,
serve
ad-hoc queries at low latency, and
persist
fresh, consistent results to Apache Iceberg™ or any other downstream system.
Try it out in 60 seconds
Install RisingWave standalone mode:
curl -L https://risingwave.com/sh
|
sh
To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see
Quick Start
.
Stream, Store, and Query — All in One
RisingWave delivers a full
end-to-end streaming data platform
— combining real-time processing with built-in storage and open-format persistence.
It supports:
Ingestion:
Ingest millions of events per second from streaming and batch sources.
Stream processing:
Perform real-time incremental processing to join and analyze live data with historical tables.
Delivery:
Deliver fresh, consistent results to data lakes (e.g., Apache Iceberg™) or any destination.
What sets RisingWave apart is its integrated storage engine:
Online serving:
Row-based storage optimized for point and range queries with single-digit millisecond latency.
Offline persistence:
Built-in Apache Iceberg™ integration for low-cost, durable storage with open access for external query engines.
With RisingWave, real-time data isn’t just processed — it’s stored, queried, and shared across your entire stack.
Key design decisions
RisingWave is designed to be easier to use and more cost-efficient:
PostgreSQL compatibility
Seamless integration:
Connects via the PostgreSQL wire protocol, working with psql, JDBC, and any Postgres tool.
Expressive SQL:
Supports structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data with a familiar SQL dialect.
No manual state tuning:
Eliminates complex state management configurations.
S3 as primary storage
RisingWave stores tables, materialized views, and internal states of stream processing jobs in S3 (or equivalent object storage), providing:
High performance:
Optimized for complex queries, including joins and time windowing.
Fast recovery:
Restores from system failures within seconds.
Dynamic scaling
:
Instantly adjusts resources to handle workload spikes.
Elastic disk cache
Beyond caching hot data in memory, RisingWave supports
elastic disk cache
, a powerful performance optimization that uses local disks or EBS for efficient data caching. This minimizes access to S3, lowering processing latency and cutting S3 access costs.
Apache Iceberg™ native support
RisingWave
natively integrates with Apache Iceberg™
, enabling continuous ingestion of streaming data into Iceberg tables. It can also read directly from Iceberg, perform automatic compaction, and maintain table health over time. Since Iceberg is an open table format, results are accessible by other query engines — making storage not only cost-efficient, but interoperable by design.
In what use cases does RisingWave excel?
RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases:
Streaming analytics
: Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring.
Event-driven applications
: Devel

• **up2isomorphism** 认为当前已经有太多类似工具，对人们继续涌入这个领域表示不解，暗示市场可能已经饱和。
• **jsumrall** 对RisingWave和Materialize表示了初步的好感，尤其对RisingWave团队有正面印象。不过最终选择了ClickHouse，因为其物化视图功能易于设置且性能良好，相比之下Timescale虽然性能不错但需要更多专业知识。
• **synthc** 希望了解RisingWave在实际生产环境中的表现，表明目前缺乏相关经验报告。
• **rubenvanwyk** 对RisingWave的实际用例感到好奇，特别是除了实时分析和可观察性之外，是否还有人将其用于增量视图维护（如在Postgres中）。
• **vivzkestrel** 提出一个基础性问题，即在什么情况下应该选择RisingWave或Kafka这样的系统，而不是传统的Redis PubSub系统。
• **shepardrtc** 对RisingWave的架构图表示赞赏，并询问使用了什么工具来制作。
• **esafak** 对RisingWave作为基于Rust的Flink简化版表示疑问，质疑其是否真的更简单。
• **acjohnson55** 直接比较RisingWave和Materialize，希望了解两者之间的优劣。

补充讨论：
• 关于RisingWave的生产环境经验报告较少，用户对其实际表现存在疑问（synthc）。
• 用户对RisingWave的实际应用场景有不同看法，有人关注其在Postgres中增量视图维护的潜力（rubenvanwyk）。
• 基础性比较，如与传统Redis PubSub的对比，显示出对何时选择复杂系统与简单系统的困惑（vivzkestrel）。
• 架构图的制作工具引发关注，显示出对技术展示方式的兴趣（shepardrtc）。
• RisingWave与Materialize的直接对比显示出用户在选择类似工具时的困惑，尤其是简化程度和功能强弱的权衡（acjohnson55, esafak）。

争议焦点：
• RisingWave是否真的比其他工具（如Flink、Materialize）更简单易用，且能满足复杂需求。
• 在何种情况下应该选择RisingWave这样的系统，而不是使用传统的简单系统如Redis PubSub。

data.title: The End of Windows 10: a toolkit for community repair groups
data.author: T-A
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在不受支持的硬件上运行Windows 11与Linux等其他操作系统的优劣对比，以及操作系统过时后的处理方式。

不同观点：
• ivraatiems认为，对于大多数人来说，即使是最简单的Linux发行版也有较高的学习曲线。相比之下，在不受支持的硬件上安装Windows 11更加方便，因为驱动程序通常可以通过Windows Update获得，且操作相对简单。虽然一年后需要手动更新，但这比处理Linux的各种问题要容易得多。
• veeti批评微软在Windows 11中对处理器和TPM的要求是任意的，不符合其在可持续发展和减少电子废物方面的承诺。他认为微软应该采取更环保的措施。
• userbinator提到Windows 11及其前身的隐私问题，并指出仍有用户群体支持旧版本的Windows，甚至为其开发驱动程序。
• concinds认为强迫用户升级到Windows 11是不必要的，因为旧系统的浏览器仍然可以接收更新。他主张不要恐慌性地让人们升级，并指出对于非技术用户而言，切换到Linux是不可行的。
• ksynwa询问Windows 11是否有类似于Windows 10 LTSC/IoT版本的精简版，以去除不必要的功能和反特性。
• user_7832指出Windows 10的长期支持版本（LTSC IoT）将支持到2032年，并提到获取该版本的合法授权可能需要一些技巧。他认为安装LTSC IoT版本与安装Linux一样具有挑战性。
• Am4TIfIsER0ppos认为即使微软停止支持，用户也可以继续使用旧系统，不会有“终止开关”直接让系统无法使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该在不受支持的硬件上运行操作系统，以及哪种操作系统更适合普通用户。
• 讨论中涉及了操作系统的安全更新、驱动程序支持、用户技术水平以及环保问题。
• 有人提出微软对硬件的要求可能并不完全基于技术需求，而是出于其他商业或市场考虑。
• 关于LTSC版本的讨论揭示了一些高级用户如何规避主流操作系统限制的策略。

data.title: CP/M creator Gary Kildall's memoirs released as free download
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Gary Kildall的回忆录近日作为免费下载发布，他是CP/M操作系统的创建者，被誉为开创了硅谷初创文化的重要人物。其子女表示，Kildall的故事展示了个人如何在技术领域开辟新道路。Kildall是数字研究公司（Digital Research Inc.）的创始人，CP/M曾是20世纪70年代和80年代初广泛使用的操作系统。他的创新和企业家精神对后来的科技行业产生了深远影响。回忆录提供了关于早期计算机历史和他个人经历的珍贵视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gary Kildall的贡献及其历史地位，以及其未发表回忆录的发布和影响。

不同观点：
• pavlov认为Gary Kildall是个人电脑行业的创始人之一，但大众并不熟悉他的名字。他批评了关于Kildall错失机会的传说，强调Kildall对技术的深远贡献及其创新理念，如开源思想和源代码共享。
• skibz希望Kildall能与Bill Gates和Steve Jobs一样被大众熟知，强调他的成就不可小觑，并提供了维基百科链接以支持其观点。
• bane回忆了自己在印刷公司使用GEM和MS-DOS等系统的经历，指出微软最终垄断了市场，而GEM未能发展出类似的软件生态系统。
• 1vuio0pswjnm7指出Kildall的回忆录只有部分章节发布，认为这有点吊人胃口，并提到Kildall的酗酒问题可能影响其历史评价。
• hackmack10认为Kildall的子女不应删除其部分作品，认为公开其与酗酒斗争的经历可能帮助有类似问题的人。

补充讨论：
• mdp和indigodaddy提供了Kildall回忆录的电子书链接，并讨论了文件质量和清理问题。
• heymijo推荐了Internet History Podcast中关于Kildall的节目，认为其详细讲述了微软如何在PC革命中获取最大价值。
• csense分享了Kildall在1975年为CP/M编写BIOS的轶事，强调了当时技术工作的简约和高效。
• garganzol和achairapart提到Kildall回忆录第二部分未发布，质疑项目是否被放弃或因内容问题未公开。

争议的焦点：
• Kildall的历史地位是否被低估及其回忆录发布的完整性问题。
• Kildall个人生活中的酗酒问题是否应被公开讨论及其对历史评价的影响。

data.title: Hundred Rabbits – Low-tech living while sailing the world
data.author: 0xCaponte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要更新了2025年多个月份的活动和进展，主要围绕船艇维护、航行计划和项目开发。文章提及了对船只Teapot和Pino的维修工作，包括重新粉刷船体和水线下的修理。团队在San Juan Islands航行，并在Blakely Island与社区成员会面。他们还进行了多项技术项目，如Uxn虚拟机的文档更新和游戏Oquonie的发布。此外，Devine开始撰写一本关于Uxn的书，并参与了游戏开发和艺术活动。文章还提到了天气对航行计划的影响和日常生活细节，以及本月的读书俱乐部书目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕100 Rabbits（Hundred Rabbits）集体及其技术、生活方式和理念的讨论

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏] 许多人表达了对100 Rabbits的赞赏，尤其是他们的ORCA音乐软件和整体的低技术、可持续生活方式。用户[rwhaling]分享了ORCA的视频和教程，称赞其为“非凡的工具”。[Mr_Eri_Atlov]认为100 Rabbits是“最成功的太阳朋克例子”，强调其在可持续性和创造力方面的贡献。[QRY]表示他们的工作启发了他如何使自己的技术更具弹性并减少依赖。[fitsumbelay]和[rezmason]也对该集体的创造力和能量表示钦佩。

• [技术路径的对比] 用户[jvanderbot]对比了100 Rabbits的“低技术/自力更生技术”与更传统的技术路径（如Forth语言），指出100 Rabbits更注重叙述性和虚拟机栈，而非回收或再利用的硬件技术。他认为这与自己所处的“Forth”技术谱系不同。

• [生活方式与哲学] 用户[periodjet]引用了100 Rabbits的哲学，讨论了文明崩溃的不可避免性，并强调了适应新现实的必要性。他还提到对抗规范暴力、法西斯主义、殖民主义和白人至上主义的重要性，呼吁以谦卑和 compassion（同情心）面对个人和集体的黑暗面。

• [技术与独立性] 用户[xrd]提到对AI能源消耗的关注，并认为100 Rabbits在帆船和UXN上的实践为如何在考虑功耗的情况下生活和工作提供了很好的例子。[QRY]进一步讨论了实现技术独立性的方法，如拥有自己的技术栈、离线工作和不断测试故障模式。

• [启发与未来计划] 用户[agentultra]表示自己受到了100 Rabbits的启发，正在努力获得帆船驾驶执照，并计划在未来更多地参与低功耗、易修复的计算机项目。[Duanemclemore]则表示100 Rabbits的生活方式和关系理念激励了自己，甚至开玩笑说如果“脱离社会”，会在不列颠哥伦比亚省的海岸边过上“隐居”生活。

补充讨论：
• [寻找类似项目] 用户[aosaigh]询问是否有其他类似的离网低技术项目或网站，并表示有兴趣探索更多这样的项目。[Conscat]提到通过Twitter上的#ORCΛ标签首次发现了100 Rabbits，并推荐其他人也去了解。

• [过去的相关讨论] 用户[dang]提供了多个与100 Rabbits相关的Hacker News讨论链接，涵盖了从技术失败性、离网生活到天气软件等多个主题，进一步扩展了讨论的背景和范围。

争议焦点：
• 100 Rabbits的技术路径选择引起了部分讨论，尤其是其更注重虚拟机栈而非回收硬件技术的做法，与传统的低技术/自力更生技术路径有所不同。用户[jvanderbot]对此提出了质疑和对比。

44561516.article_content:
home
log
Receive monthly updates via our
RSS feed
, or by signing up to our monthly
newsletter
.
2025
01-2025
02-2025
03-2025
04-2025
05-2025
06-2025
June 2025
100r.co
, updated
costs
,
hauling out
,
united states
and
teapot gelcoat
. Added
san juan islands
.
Rabbit Waves
, added all content links to the main page, released a new page called
Boatswain's Call
.
Orca
, embedded runtime in the
reference guide
.
Left
, made lots of little improvements and optimizations!
Solresol
, learnt
some profanities
in a musical conlang?
For a few days, Pino became a
land creature
, living on stilts, while we scrubbed and re-painted the lower part of the hull. Our propeller had a bit of a wobble, which we
hope
is now corrected. We also battled with the
old wheel quadrant
and were finally able to remove it, at least a part of it. Boaters have frequently helped us while we were in boatyards, and we are finally able to pay it forward. We offered both advice to those who asked and lent tools to folks that needed them. It felt nice.
Teapot
's new bottom has seen water for the first time, the new gelcoat will allow us to take it around into bays for many more years to come.
We spent many June days working on both
Turnip Complete
(
Uxn
book) and the enhanced version of the
Victoria to Sitka Logbook
, with frequent breaks to enjoy the
beautiful places
we found ourselves in.
The beginning of our sailing season has been very blustery, allowing for some good sailing, but also often forcing us to wait at anchor for clement weather. Later, we sailed through the
San Juan Islands
to meet up with some Merveillans on Blakely Island. We are very grateful to be part of a community of such kind, curious, and generous people. The image that was drawn for this month's update represents cooperation between members of
Merveilles
.
Book Club:
This month we are reading
Ill Met By Moonlight
by Sarah A. Hoyt,
Silmarillion
by J.R.R Tolkien and
Girl's Last Tour
by Tsukumizu.
May 2025
100r.co
, updated
water
and
Oquonie
.
Modal
, the interpreter was
ported to Uxn
!
Uxntal
, the
documentation
has been completely redone!
Hakum
, added
page 7
and
page 8
of
Sabotage Study
.
Oquonie
was released on the
Playdate Catalog
this month! We'd like to thank everyone who sent us photos of their progress in the game, it has been nice to follow along. The game is kind of our first official release on a modern handheld platform, and we're happy to see that Uxn roms run well on it! It might be one of the first original Playdate games implemented that way?
In other news, Devine started working on a book, the working title is "
Turnip Complete
". The goal is to write a complete and stand-alone implementation guide for the Uxn virtual machine and devices, along with some example programs and thoughts about playful computery things. We might have something to show for it come autumn, maybe.
We've left
Victoria
for the summer, and are falling back into the groove of waking up at dusk to catch the tide. We have a quick haul out lined up, and afterward we'll be sailing around the Gulf Islands until the fall. We have lots of projects to finish up these next couple of months and can't wait to share them with you.
We share photos of life aboard throughout the month on our little
photo site
, if you're curious to see what the daily life aboard Pino is like.
Book Club:
This month we are reading
Artemis
by Andy Weir,
Gardening Without Work: For the Aging, the Busy and the Indolent
by Ruth Stout and
A History of Thinking on Paper
by Roland Allen.
April 2025
100r.co
, updated
water
,
ditch bag
,
woodstove installation
, and added new photos and information on
first aid kit
.
Rabbit Waves
, updated
Triangular Bandages
with animated gifs, and
First-Aid kit
with new med suggestions (also appended a .txt list of meds and their intended use).
Hakum
, began a new comic sequence named
Sabotage Study
(not yet completed).
Orca
, modified the behavior of the lowercase-j operator to allow for jumpers to grow.
Solresol
, improved the documentation.
Uxntal
, improved the documentation.
The weather is getting warmer, which is perfect for airing out
Pino
's lockers, and drying off moldy clothes and tools. Anything stored in the v-berth lockers, below the waterline, suffer from extreme wetness. It is a very, very annoying fact of boat life, but there is really no way to bring good air flow in those spaces. We scrubbed the lockers clean, parted with items we no longer needed, and sent two laptops to the recycler.
In last month's update, we mentioned Flickjam, a game jam based on Increpare's
Flickgame
. We received a total of
27 entries
! They're really fun, and all playable in the browser.
Devine's jam entry
is about a very adorable rabbit learning to play the word "rabbit" on a xylophone in
Solresol
.
Devine spent some time off the computer,
skating
and
folding paper

data.title: Row Polymorphic Programming
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了行多态（row polymorphism）在处理现实世界中的杂乱数据时的优势，特别是在业务逻辑和数据结构定义中。行多态允许在类型签名中对记录类型中的字段进行抽象，从而实现数据结构的灵活定义和操作，如记录的连接和新字段的选择。与普通记录类型相比，行类型更加灵活，可以根据模式（schema）动态调整。文章通过家具和房间的例子展示了行多态的实际应用，如计算房间剩余面积，避免了为每种数据类型手动实现接口的麻烦。行多态通过类型安全的反射操作，简化了复杂数据结构的处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“行多态性”（Row Polymorphism）及其在不同编程语言中的应用和争议的讨论。

不同观点：
• [owlstuffing] 认为行多态性类似于结构化类型（Structural Typing），如TypeScript和Go语言中的接口系统。他进一步解释了参数类型和结果类型的协变与逆变性质，并提到Java中的Manifold项目作为增强类型系统的例子。
   
• [aerzen] 作为Rust程序员，尝试理解行多态性，将其类比为Rust中的泛型函数，这些函数可以对具有某些字段的结构体进行操作。他提到对ML家族语言中的多箭头符号感到困惑。

• [daxfohl] 希望有一种方法能够安全地将行多态记录提升为命名记录类型，特别是当编译器可以确定它具有所有必需字段时，但目前尚未见到有语言提供这种功能。

• [skybrian] 质疑行多态性的必要性，询问它能实现哪些通过Go语言中的泛型函数和切片无法实现的功能。

• [constantcrying] 提到Matlab有一种特殊的数据类型——单元数组（cell array），可以存储任意类型的2D数据，正好符合讨论中的用例。

• [malcolmgreaves] 认为一些有经验的程序员对类型系统的抱怨实际上是因为缺乏行多态性或相关的结构化子类型，尽管他们可能没有相关的技术词汇来准确表达这一点。

• [moron4hire] 提到名义类型（Nominal Typing），并认为接口不仅仅是方法和字段的集合，它们还编码了语义，否则会导致逻辑错误，如用枪解雇员工或把他们放进窑炉。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是行多态性是否优于名义类型，以及它能否提供比现有语言特性更多的表达能力。
• 另一个讨论点是行多态性在编译时的安全性和实用性，如[daxfohl]提到的编译器提升问题。
• 不同语言背景的程序员对行多态性的理解和接受程度不同，如[aerzen]和[skybrian]的疑问所示。

44563867.article_content:
Sometimes, especially when dealing with business logic, we have to
deal with data that comes in from the real world, or elsewhere,
naturally very messily typed, leading to nasty type signatures and
messes of macros or code generation to build data structures from a
schema. Row polymorphism can help us by abstracting over the fields
contained in a record type in the type signature, letting us define
records based on data, concatenate records together, and define
functions that are generic across any record containing the required
fields, all without macros.
This article is inspired by my work on implementing the
Brown
Benchmark for Table Types
1
for my
Structures
2
library, an update for which will be
released soon, providing a much more comprehensive collection of types
for row-polymorphic programming.
What is Row Polymorphism
At time of writing, the
Wikipedia page
for row polymorphism starts with:
In programming language type theory, row polymorphism is a kind of
polymorphism that allows one to write programs that are polymorphic on
row types such as record types and polymorphic variants.
leading into some text dense with mathematical notation that doesn't
do much in explaining what any of this
looks
like, and what the
hell does "polymorphic on row types" even mean?
Consider a basic
record
in Idris as an example:
record
ImACat
where
constructor
MkCat
name
:
String
age
:
Nat
meows_a_lot
:
Bool
This certainly seems like it might fit the bill, it says
record
right there, and the wikipedia snippet
did
mention records. But what are these "row types"?
Row Types
"Row Type" and "Record Type" are sometimes used interchangeably in
this corner of type theory. While "record" may be a somewhat more
intuitive name for someone approaching this from the perspective of many
popular programming languages, we will mostly be using the name "Row
Type", as it will make more sense in the tabular data context that will
serve as framing for this article.
Imagine some tabular data, say a table in a database or a spread
sheet. Tabular data is composed of a 2d grid of rows and columns,
typically with each column having a name and potentially a type
constraint on the values in that column. Consider this example:
Cats
name â String
age â Nat
meows_a_lot â Bool
Cricket
11
False
Cookie-Dough
4
True
Mango
0
False
Creampuff
5
True
"Row Types" are constructions for describing individual rows in such
a structure
3
. They are parameterized by a list of
(label, Type)
pairs, represented by the header of the table
and referred to as a schema. We can see that the labels and types in our
Cats
table are identical to the fields of our
ImACat
record from earlier. As such, each row in the table
can be thought of as an instance of the
ImACat
record, and
the table itself as a list of such records.
That dependence on a schema, a piece of data describing the structure
of the type, makes row types a bit more flexible, as well as a bit more
complicated. We can perform the usual operations, like accessing a given
column in a row by name, analogous to field access like calling
name
on value of
ImACat
. More interestingly,
we can also perform new operations that enable a sort of limited,
type-safe reflection over row types, such as selecting a specific set of
columns from a row to produce a new row type, or concatenating the
schemas of two rows to create a new type expressing the result of
joining the rows.
The Mysterious Row
Polymorphism
Imagine you are helping your friend move and they need to figure out
what furniture will fit in what rooms. The previous occupant of their
new place has graciously provided a table containing the length and
width of each room, and their furniture supplier has provided a table
detailing the lengths, widths, and heights of the bounding cuboids for
each piece of furniture:
Rooms

length â Double
width â Double
Bedroom
3.65
3.35
Living Room
4.87
3.35
Dining Room
2.44
2.44
Kitchen
3.35
2.44
Bathroom
3.65
2.44
Furniture
item â String
length â Double
width â Double
height â Double
Dresser
1.00
0.60
0.76
Bed
2.00
1.50
0.50
Nightstand
0.60
0.48
0.75
Dinner Table
1.80
0.90
0.80
TV Stand
1.93
0.42
0.90
Coffee Table
1.81
0.81
0.46
One thing that's going to be critical to determine is how much floor
space is left in a room after the furniture's been placed in it. After
all, a room isn't of much use if there's not even enough free floor
space to stand in it. You notice that both of these tables contain the
information needed to calculate the available area and the foot prints
of the furniture, the
length
and
width
columns.
Its tempting to define a
Room
data type and a
Furniture
data type containing each table's respective
columns as fields, and describe the area/footprint via an
Area
interface. However, this approach has several
drawbacks. It requires implementing the interface manually for each data
type

error, such as inadvertently using the wrong field to calculate the

data.author: jasong
data.article_summary: 《Embrace the Grind: 15 Years of Building Jefit》文章回顾了Jefit应用过去15年的发展历程。创始人最初只是为了解决自己健身追踪的难题，在家中用笔记本开始了这个项目，并未预期它会持续如此之久。最初借了几千美元维持生活，逐渐构建出一个帮助人们保持健身动力的平台。经过数月编程，Jefit开始吸引用户，并于2010年正式成立公司。在缺乏资金和宣传的情况下，团队凭借信念逐步扩展。为了更大发展，创始人举家迁至硅谷，经过两年重组，团队逐渐壮大。尽管面临用户流失和产品失误等挑战，Jefit坚持提升质量，不断改进平台。在15周年之际，Jefit推出了多项更新，包括更现代的界面和更智能的功能，继续专注于质量控制，感谢用户的长期支持。

44568761.article_content:
Embrace the Grind: 15 Years of Building Jefit
The Start of Something I Didn't Expect to Last 15 Years
Fifteen years ago, Jefit wasn't a company. It wasn't even a business idea.
It was just a project I started in my dad's living room in North Carolina, fresh out of college, working from my own laptop.
I was broke and unsure about the future, frustrated by how hard it was to track workouts. There was no easy way to stay consistent or see real progress. I wasn't chasing a startup dream, just building something to keep me accountable.
I borrowed a few thousand dollars from friends to cover basic expenses, food, gas, nothing fancy. I was young and had little to lose. If this project helped me stay on track, maybe it could help someone else too.
What I didn't realize was that once I started building, I'd be committing the next 15 years of my life to it. After a few months of coding, something clicked. I started hearing from others, people like me, who wanted structure, progress, and accountability. That's when I began taking it seriously.
This wasn't just about tracking sets and reps. It was about motivation. Consistency. Long-term commitment. That's when the idea of a
social workout platform
took shape, something to help people stay on track, together.
On July 15, 2010, I officially incorporated Jefit. I was still working 18 to 19 hours a day, coding, fixing bugs, and dreaming. A few months later, real users started showing up, and for the first time, I made just enough to repay the small loan from my friend. I even hired my first full-time teammate. He didn't have a car, so I drove him to my dad's house every morning. It wasn't glamorous, but it felt like the beginning of something real.
Building With What We Had
For six years, I built with a tiny, bootstrapped team, hiring one person at a time. We had no funding or PR, just belief. Belief that people who train with purpose deserved better tools.
Eventually, I knew we needed to grow. But to do that, I had to take a big risk.
I was raising a two-year-old son with my wife.
My team in North Carolina didn't want to relocate. If I moved, I'd be starting from scratch, with no team, no network, and just a fragile startup.
Still, I believed if I could find the right people, people who shared our values, we could build something lasting. So I moved my company and family to
Silicon Valley
.
Starting over wasn't instant or easy. It took two years to regroup and start hiring the kind of teammates this vision needed, while I kept building with a few remote teammates. It was slow. It was hard. But step by step, things came together.
Looking back, it was worth every step.
Discipline Starts With the Team
Today our team is still small, but incredibly capable, a tight-knit group of people who came from across the country to join this mission.
Many share the same traits that started Jefit: a love for training, an obsession with quality, and the discipline to build something meaningful.
Daily workouts. Dogfooding our own product. Reading user comments together. That's just how we operate, regardless of title. Everyone participates. Everyone trains. Everyone cares.
Our walls are lined with live metrics, NPS reviews, and feedback. Because we don't just build for users, we build
with
them.
It's the culture I always dreamed of. And the move to Silicon Valley made it possible.
Learning the Hard Way
This journey hasn't been easy. I've made mistakes, some small, some nearly fatal.
During the COVID lockdowns, we lost over half our users overnight. But we didn't panic. We adapted, and even grew the team.
More than 50 VC firms passed on us, even with 20-30% year-over-year growth. We weren't seen as a "sexy" deal. So we kept building our way.
I made product mistakes too, chasing features while neglecting quality. That led to product and engineering debt.
One of the hardest things to hear was, "That's just Jefit being Jefit." It meant bugs or quirks we hadn't fixed. I knew it came from frustration, but also something deeper:
loyalty
.
People stuck with us. And that's exactly why we're raising the bar now.
What's Next
As we mark Jefit's 15-year anniversary, we're not just looking back, we're building forward.
We've modernized the platform from the inside out:
A refreshed mobile app interface
Faster, frictionless logging and log management
Reorganized progress reports and charting
New goal-setting and tracking tools
Smarter machine-generated workouts
Behind the scenes, we've upgraded our backend infrastructure, delivering faster network response, more secure syncing, and a stronger foundation for AI-driven features.
Whether you build your own plans or prefer a guided path, your experience will feel more seamless, responsive, and personalized.
And through it all,
quality control
will stay at the center of everything we do.
To Everyone on This Journey
Whether you logged your first workout yesterday or your thousandth last year, thank you for choosing Jefit.

44568761.article_summary: 《Embrace the Grind: 15 Years of Building Jefit》文章回顾了Jefit应用过去15年的发展历程。创始人最初只是为了解决自己健身追踪的难题，在家中用笔记本开始了这个项目，并未预期它会持续如此之久。最初借了几千美元维持生活，逐渐构建出一个帮助人们保持健身动力的平台。经过数月编程，Jefit开始吸引用户，并于2010年正式成立公司。在缺乏资金和宣传的情况下，团队凭借信念逐步扩展。为了更大发展，创始人举家迁至硅谷，经过两年重组，团队逐渐壮大。尽管面临用户流失和产品失误等挑战，Jefit坚持提升质量，不断改进平台。在15周年之际，Jefit推出了多项更新，包括更现代的界面和更智能的功能，继续专注于质量控制，感谢用户的长期支持。

data.title: CoCo1 composite video
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者为Tandy CoCo电脑添加复合视频输出的改造过程。CoCo原仅通过RF射频输出视频，图像质量较差。作者发现其视频电路已生成复合信号，但未引出到实际端口。通过参考Barry Nelson和Martin H. Goodman的设计，作者使用两个2n2222晶体管构成达林顿对来放大信号，并通过RCA接口输出复合视频。作者最初在面包板上测试电路，随后设计并批量制作了小型PCB板。整个过程简单直接，并成功实现了更清晰的视频输出。作者还提到未来可能使用更先进的芯片或方案进一步改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对CoCo 2进行的复合视频修改及其技术细节

不同观点：
• msarnoff：成功对CoCo 2进行了复合视频修改，结合了多种现有的修改方案，并在板上面安装了一个与RF调制器占位相同的大小板。虽然找到MC1372芯片有难度，但使用NTE855作为替代品解决了问题。音频/视频输出使用了3.5mm TRS插孔，避免在机箱上打额外的孔，只需要一根廉价的3.5mm立体声到RCA的线缆。不过，缺少详细的原理图，最终的连接是手动完成的。

• alnwlsn：也进行了类似的修改，尝试了与原帖（msarnoff）相似的电路，但并不满意最终的结果，并分享了一个个人网页链接（包含具体修改内容和细节），暗示可能有改进或不同的方法。

• mikewarot：从技术角度解释了电路中2n2222晶体管对的作用，指出其作为双射极跟随器具有电压一致性增益，但能够去除信号中的一些偏置。这可能是对msarnoff和alnwlsn讨论中电路设计问题的一个技术性补充。

补充讨论：
• msarnoff和alnwlsn的实际操作结果存在差异，可能与具体电路设计或实现细节有关，alnwlsn明确表示对结果不满意，并提供了另外的参考链接。
• mikewarot的评论提供了技术分析，解释了电路中特定元件的功能，帮助理解电路设计中的关键点。
• 争议焦点在于最终的实现效果，alnwlsn对msarnoff的方案提出了隐含的质疑，表明有改进空间或不同偏好。

44571908.article_content:
When I got the CoCo, one of the big problems was the super-smeary, snowy video on the RF-out. Even though composite video is generated internally by the video circuitry of the computer, Tandy didn’t end up breaking it out to an actual port. Lots of other 8-bit machines of the era are in the same boat. Luckily, adding a composite video port to the CoCo is very straightforward! So straightforward, in fact, that I did it twice.
Theory
As I said just now,
the Motorola 6847 VDG
already generates a composite video signal (by way of the
MC1372 modulator
transforming it from something-like-YCbCr into composite) and sends it to the RF modulator, which encodes it and the sound with the channel frequency. This is accomplished through some kind of fancy radio math that is scary, but thankfully I don’t have to understand it.
This RF signal is transmitted into the antenna input of a television set, and then you can tune into channel 3 or 4 to watch your CoCo work. There’s a great explanation of how RF video encoding works
in this now-classic Cathode Ray Dude YouTube video about NES RF
, including some inadvertent operation of a pirate TV station.
Since I already have composite coming out of the internal chips, I’ll just snipe it from where it comes from and get it to the TV directly. Easy, right?
This project started in 2019, which you may note is not the current year. This is one of those projects that has taken me a really long time to get to this point.
Discovery
My first step was to see if someone else had made a composite mod. Composite is ‘good enough’ for most of my old computers; I have a lot of composite monitors and TVs lying around the place, and it’s probably fairly future-proof. Even new LCD TVs sold at Walmart still have an AV jack in them, and
cheap AV-to-HDMI adapters
will probably keep existing until I’m in the ground.
There is the amazing
CoCoVGA 6847 replacement
, but it’s quite a bit of money to spend on a CoCo that doesn’t even have a working keyboard yet. Plus, I know how I work. It would probably end up getting used in
one of the PC-6001s
anyway.
I found
this circuit on Hackaday’s community portal, done by Barry Nelson
. It’s an enhancement of
a circuit from 1983 designed by Martin H. Goodman
.
My theory is a little thin, but the two 2n2222 transistors in the middle seem to form
a Darlington pair
- a common design for an el-cheapo amplifier. From what I can tell, this takes the attenuated composite-video signal from the 6847 (on pin 12) and beefs it up so it can provide enough current to satisfy the demand from the television. Then we take the beefier composite video signal, and put it out on some RCA jacks. Thanks, transistors!
This output-level amplification is one of the services provided by
the THS7374 chip used in my rough Famicom composite video mod
. I thought about reusing that board – I had plenty left over – but I figured following this design might teach me something.
U12 in this diagram is
not
the 6847. You may recall from
an earlier entry on the CoCo
that the 6847 has a little friend called
the MC1372P video mixer
, which takes the raw chroma(e) and luma signals from the 6847 and mixes them into composite video.
It’s really nice when the datasheets provide me with a diagram. Remember that composite video is really the base signal for what we call “RF-out;” it just hasn’t been put onto an actual channel yet. The RF modulator box on the board still needs to take that signal and mix it into a TV channel (3 or 4) so the TV can understand it.
I started off doing this circuit on a protoboard, but then I wasn’t pleased with how it looked. At the same time, I was already sending off a very large order to JLCPCB, so I tacked it on the order.
I could definitely have made this board much smaller. The 10k fine-tuning potentiometer and the massive footprint for a measly 0.1µF capacitor are the dominant elements. Even so, the resulting board is still so small that it was easy to panelize a bunch of them and send them out for order.
Dechunked
The panelization was pretty cool! I got back five boards that had been scored, and I could snap them apart into little boards. Each of the five ‘big boards’ carried 12 little boards on them, so I ended up with a total of 60 CoCo composite boards. One or two were damaged in manufacture (scratched) and JLCPCB refunded me for them before shipping them out.
After a few minutes of snapping apart boards on my kitchen table, I had a soup of PCBs and a CoCo composite board to work on.
There were actually a lot of different boards tacked onto this order. Don’t peek too closely! You’ll spoil future projects. Err, past projects. Maybe a little of both.
After a few minutes of surface-mount and through-hole soldering, the first test board was assembled. I realized a little late in production that I didn’t have any 0.1µF electrolytic capacitors on hand, so instead it got one of a pile of 0.1µF unpolarized ceramic caps from my hoard. Oh well, it still looks… alright, if a litt

data.title: Trying Guix: A Nixer's impressions
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章作者是一位长期使用Nix的开发者，尝试了Guix后分享了他的体验和对比。Guix和Nix在底层包管理机制上类似，但整体生态和架构有显著差异。Guix基于Scheme语言，不同于Nix的"一个大结构"的包管理方式，Guix采用命名空间的Scheme模块。这意味着在Guix中切换版本需要通过"guix pull"命令重新构建Guix，无法像Nix一样直接在代码中引入不同版本的包。此外，Guix严格遵循自由软件原则，不包含专有软件，用户可能需要使用"nonguix"来获取某些硬件支持。作者虽然未成功配置完桌面环境，但对Guix的独特架构和设计留下了深刻印象，并计划继续尝试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Guix与Nix的比较、Niri独特的设计、系统管理工具（如systemd与Shepherd）的争议、以及Linux生态系统中的一些技术问题。

不同观点：
• abrookewood对Niri（一个可滚动平铺的Wayland compositor）表示兴趣，认为其无限水平条带的桌面范式独特，但不确定是否需要。
• idlip认为需要更多对比性文章来减少偏见，指出Guix生态系统的主要问题是缺乏基础设施和志愿者，并相信如果解决这些问题，Guix会有显著改善。
• CBLT分享了自己在老旧笔记本上运行Guix的困难经历，最终搁置了项目，直到考虑建立distcc集群。
• hamandcheese表示因为Guix不支持macOS而犹豫尝试。
• hardwaresofton批评Guix坚持使用Shepherd而非systemd，认为这是其无法普及的原因，并指出自己在使用nonguix解决网络问题时的技术困难。

补充讨论：
• peterldowns对Guix的文档表示赞赏，但指出需要Scheme知识可能成为入门障碍，同时批评Nix语言的复杂性。
• pkulak对flakes的争议表示兴趣，希望了解更多关于flakes为何被认为是无意义的原因。
• guilhas对Nix和Guix都有好感，但也指出它们在图形卡处理和系统更新方面的共同问题，并提出通过使用不同频道来增加系统稳定性的建议。

争议焦点：
• Guix坚持使用Shepherd而非主流的systemd，用户hardwaresofton认为这是Guix无法普及的原因，而其他人可能有不同看法。
• Nix和Guix在图形卡处理和系统更新上的问题，guilhas指出这些基本功能的缺失，并与传统包管理方式的差异引发了讨论。

44569032.article_content:
Trying Guix: A Nixer's Impressions
2025-07-06
People occasionally ask me how I think Guix compares to Nix. Let me set the stage: I've been using Nix for many years, have large projects using Nix, used to be very active in the Nix community, and even wrote
multiple
Nix language interpreters, so I'd say that I'm at least
fairly comfortable
with Nix.
I'm also one of those people who live in Emacs. I'm no stranger to Lisps (although my experience with Scheme is limited) and am very fond of them. It feels natural that people ask me about my views on Guix.
The thing is: I haven't actually ever used Guix, so I just don't
know
. But there's an easy way to find out: let's try it! So that's what I did this weekend.
Here are a few things I ran into and found noteworthy. My goal was to take my
Unchartevice
laptop with its strange Zhaoxin x86_64-compatible CPU and see if I could get all the way to my standard
niri
desktop. There's no overarching point here, just observations a user of one or the other system might find interesting.
Spoiler:
I didn't manage, but I saw a lot of interesting stuff. Knowing myself, I'll probably keep trying when some free time shows up.
A quick note before we begin: Technically, Guix uses a fork of the Nix daemon for the low-level primitives of functional package management (the
Nix
Guix Store, derivations, substitutions, and all that stuff are
basically
the same). The projects forked a long time ago, and development has diverged significantly since then. The similarities end here, however: Guix is not "just" Nix with Scheme â it's a complete alternative ecosystem built in parallel on top of the same foundational infrastructure. A mental model of "Nix with Lisp syntax" will
not
work in practice when approaching Guix.
Anyway, here we go.
nonguix
The very first thing I ran into is more political, but I must mention it, as almost everyone trying the Guix System will face this immediately.
Skip
this if you want to get straight into the technical stuff.
Guix is the GNU system, and as such takes software freedoms very seriously. Guix does not recommend and does not ship the proprietary blobs needed for most modern hardware. The FSF has
a website
that lists laptops that work without them, but it is
very
limited. The
majority
of Guix System users use something called
nonguix
that adds these blobs, giving you access to things such as wireless internet.
I don't want to make this post about the political side of software freedoms, but I had to use
nonguix
to get internet working on the machine, which had very immediate technical effects that bring me to:
Architectural Differences
A major and immediate difference between Guix and Nix is that they layer things differently. Nix works like this:
[ nix-daemon ] <-> [ Nix CLI ] <- [ Nix code ]
The brackets here are intended to signify
independence
: You can mix (to some extent) separately built nix-daemons and Nix CLIs, and you can use almost any version of Nix from the last 8 years or so to evaluate almost any Nix code (let's, please, not get into
why flakes are nonsense
why this is only "almost" true).
The Nix CLI knows nothing
1
about nixpkgs. In most Nix code, something, somewhere will
import
a commit of nixpkgs, which yields an enormous data structure lazily containing all Nix packages, and then use bits of this structure. Importing multiple nixpkgs commits is no problemâit just means that you have
two
large data structures now. In effect, this means that you can mix and match nixpkgs commits (or other Nix config) freely
within the language
, and Nix always evaluates the entire thing.
In fact, in TVL
we mix nixpkgs commits
all the time, because we track unstable releases and occasionally need to pick software from an older stable commit.
Guix doesn't work like this, and I found it very confusing at first. That's not to say it's bad â it's just different:
[ guix-daemon ] <-> [ guix CLI + profile ] <- [ Guix user code ]
As in Nix, the Guix daemon converses with the CLI over an RPC interface. The difference is that the Guix CLI runs in a fixed profile that has
all
of the packages and modules from all channels
baked in
. In contrast to Nix, the Guix package/service set is not one big data structure, but a namespaced hierarchy of Scheme modules. The Guix CLI is a Scheme environment in which packages, services and so on are available for import in user code.
This means that to change the Guix version (i.e., commit in their
monorepo
, which is the implementation of the CLI
and
of the package set, as if
NixOS/nix
and
NixOS/nixpkgs
were one) you essentially
rebuild Guix
. In Guix land, this happens through a command called
guix pull
, which ultimately yields (as I understand it) a new
guix
binary with a hardcoded profile.
This has two effects that were noticeable to me:
Switching between versions is always at least a two-step process: Rebuild Guix, then rebuild your config. You can't easily
2
, as in Nix, just import a different Guix commit in your code.
R

data.title: Firefox-patch-bin, librewolf-fix-bin AUR packages contain malware
data.author: rrampage
data.article_summary: 2025年7月16日，有恶意用户向AUR上传了包含恶意软件的软件包，这些软件包包括librewolf-fix-bin、firefox-patch-bin和zen-browser-patched-bin，它们会安装来自同一GitHub库的远程访问木马（RAT）。Arch Linux团队在发现后立即处理，并于7月18日删除了这些恶意软件包。建议安装过这些软件包的用户立即移除，并采取措施确保系统未被入侵。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Arch Linux中使用AUR（Arch User Repository）安装软件的安全性及如何提升其安全性

不同观点：
• RandyOrion强调在Arch Linux上安装软件时应优先选择官方包或官方推荐的安装方法，如果需要使用AUR，必须仔细检查PKGBUILD文件中的每一行，确保其安全，因为AUR默认不受信任。
• jabjq对如何判断是否受到恶意软件影响表示困惑，指出在没有具体恶意软件行为描述的情况下，用户难以采取行动。
• heavyset_go希望获取恶意软件包的副本以在虚拟机中进行分析，表明一些用户可能希望通过实际操作来研究恶意软件的行为。
• WD-42担心随着Arch Linux的流行，未来可能会出现更多类似安全问题，暗示用户群扩大会增加安全隐患。
• mzajc质疑这些恶意软件包的目的和用户安装的原因，指出PKGBUILD描述缺乏对“-patched”部分的解释，使用户困惑。
• lorenzohess建议开发工具帮助用户自动分析AUR包的安全性，例如显示PKGBUILD中的所有URL或自动对比更新前后的PKGBUILD文件，甚至提出使用LLM（大型语言模型）辅助分析的可能性。
• akerl_对问题仅出现在AUR邮件列表中，而未在主页、公告列表或安全列表中提及表示不解，认为信息发布渠道可能不够完善。
• npteljes认为虽然Firefox和LibreWolf很流行，但恶意软件包的影响可能有限，因为问题被及时发现，且搜索结果显示受影响范围较小。
• christophilus作为Fedora用户，表示对COPR包的安全性感到担忧，并计划进行审计，反映出不同Linux发行版的用户对第三方包管理的安全性有共同的顾虑。
• lilly-lizard指出受影响的包与流行的librewolf-bin等不同，并赞扬问题在两天内被发现，推测可能是善意用户主动检查新包的PKGBUILD文件。
• defraudbah承认过去安装了许多AUR包，担心可能已中招，但对如何防范表示无奈，同时不愿转向其他发行版如Ubuntu。
• Barrin92将AUR的安全问题比作在Craigslist上购买心脏药物，认为用户信任匿名上传者存在固有风险，并指出Arch的极简设计使得AUR非常流行，也因此带来了安全隐患。
• jchoksi建议在pacman中集成VirusTotal扫描功能，通过API自动对AUR包进行病毒扫描，并标记失败的扫描结果，以增强安全性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AUR包的信任和安全性问题，用户对如何判断和防范恶意软件包存在困惑和需求。
• 提出了多种提升AUR安全性的建议，包括自动分析工具、LLM辅助审查、VirusTotal集成等技术手段。
• 讨论中反映了不同用户对AUR依赖程度的差异，以及对安全问题的不同态度和应对方式。

[SECURITY] firefox-patch-bin, librewolf-fix-bin and zen-browser-patched-bin AUR packages contain malware

Command in DLAGENTS works in shell...
Quentin MICHAUD
18 Jul
2025
18 Jul
'25
6:53 p.m.
On the 16th of July, at around 8pm UTC+2, a malicious AUR package was
uploaded to the AUR. Two other malicious packages were uploaded by the
same user a few hours later. These packages were installing a script
coming from the same GitHub repository that was identified as a Remote
Access Trojan (RAT).
The affected malicious packages are:
-  librewolf-fix-bin
-  firefox-patch-bin
-  zen-browser-patched-bin
The Arch Linux team addressed the issue as soon as they became aware of
the situation. As of today, 18th of July, at around 6pm UTC+2, the
offending packages have been deleted from the AUR.
We strongly encourage users that may have installed one of these
packages to remove them from their system and to take the necessary
measures in order to ensure they were not compromised.

data.title: A New Geometry for Einstein's Theory of Relativity
data.author: jandrewrogers
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一组维也纳的数学家正在开发工具，以扩展爱因斯坦广义相对论的适用范围。传统相对论通过10个相互关联的微分方程描述物质和能量如何弯曲时空，但在遇到如黑洞中心奇点等非平滑几何情况时，这些方程失效。数学家Clemens Sämann和Michael Kunzinger试图找到不依赖平滑性和微分的新方法，以应对这些极端环境。他们与团队合作，重新推导了宇宙核心定理，并提出了一个新几何框架，能够处理更复杂和不规则的时空结构，旨在为相对论提供更坚实的数学基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对物理学理论（特别是广义相对论、奇点、振荡理论等）的不同理解和看法

不同观点：
• [cluckindan] 提出一种非严谨的振荡理论，认为一切存在都是振荡，这些振荡通过相互作用形成基本粒子，并最终产生质量和多维因果结构。该观点强调了我们作为系统内部观察者，无法直接体验非局部性，存在似乎是维度分离的。
  - 论据：振荡之间的共振与不谐导致高阶结构的形成，奇点中的结构崩溃会导致量子真空，进而释放无质量和非局部性的成分。

• [WCSTombs] 对文章表示赞赏，并联想到自己曾研究的关于将某些概念从平滑流形推广到"非平滑"环境的工作，特别是最优传输（optimal transport）的概念。
  - 论据：最优传输在纯数学和应用数学中未得到足够重视，本有可能成为其博士论文的主题，但由于人生选择未能继续探索。

• [Sniffnoy] 对新奇点定理的出现持怀疑态度，认为这可能不是积极的信号。根据其理解，奇点是广义相对论在极端尺度下由于缺乏量子引力理论而出现的非物理现象。
  - 争议焦点：奇点是否是真实的物理存在，还是仅仅是广义相对论在量子尺度下的缺陷表现。理想的理论应避免奇点。

• [ggdG] 质疑广义相对论是否确实告诉我们宇宙在膨胀，认为广义相对论的微分方程可以根据不同的初始条件和约束产生不同的解。
  - 论据：广义相对论本身只是提供了解决方案的框架，具体的解依赖于天文观测提供的条件和约束。

• [michaelsbradley] 提到可以用欧几里得度量来重新表述广义相对论，而非传统的闵可夫斯基度量，并提供了一个相关网站链接。
  - 补充：这种重新表述提供了一种不同的几何视角，可能对理解广义相对论有帮助。

• [kittikitti] 对文章持批评态度，认为其只是为尚未经过同行评审的理论做市场宣传，填补爱因斯坦粉丝的点击量需求。
  - 论据：希望这些数学家能够完善爱因斯坦的广义相对论，使其与现代物理学相容，而不是仅仅做一些表面文章。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对奇点和广义相对论的看法存在明显争议，一部分人认为奇点是理论缺陷的表现，另一部分人则探讨了广义相对论的不同数学表述及其物理意义。
- 对新理论的接受度和其在现代物理学中的应用前景也是讨论的重点，尤其是对新理论是否能经过实验验证并融入现有物理框架的关注。

A team of mathematicians based in Vienna is developing tools to extend the scope of general relativity.

I
n October 2015, a young mathematician named
Clemens Sämann
was flying home to Austria from a conference in Turin, Italy, when he had a chance encounter. He found himself seated beside
Michael Kunzinger
, another conference attendee. Kunzinger was a math professor at the University of Vienna, where Sämann had just started his postdoctoral research. They soon got to talking, landing on a subject Sämann had started thinking about in graduate school — whether there was a mathematical way to get around the limitations of Albert Einstein’s general theory of relativity.
Einstein’s theory defines gravity as the curvature of space-time caused by the presence of matter and energy. Since its formulation in 1915, it has held up remarkably well. Consisting of 10 interconnected differential equations, the theory describes how objects fall, how light bends, and how planets, stars and galaxies move. It tells us that the universe is expanding, and it predicted the existence of both black holes and gravitational waves a century before they were definitively observed.
But in spite of these successes, Einstein’s theory also has shortcomings. Its equations can only describe how matter curves space-time when the geometry of that space-time is smooth — with no sharp corners or cusps, no regions where it suddenly becomes jagged. Picture space-time as a flat rubber sheet, and matter as a bowling ball placed on that sheet, causing it to bend. If space-time is smooth, then this bending will be gradual.
But physicists know that’s not always true. A black hole, for instance, warps space-time more violently, causing the sheet to bend sharply until, at the black hole’s center (a so-called singularity), the curvature “blows up,” becoming infinite. Some physicists even posit that space-time doesn’t become non-smooth only at isolated singularities, but at every point. On the smallest scales, space-time might be “discrete,” or pixelated — broken up into tiny, disconnected bits in the same way that a fluid, while appearing to be a single uniform entity, is actually made up of distinct atoms and molecules.
In these situations, general relativity hits an impasse. Whenever space-time isn’t sufficiently smooth, Einstein’s equations stop working. They can no longer tell us how matter curves space-time, or how curved space-time influences matter.
That’s because the equations rely on a technique from calculus
called differentiation
that measures how quickly functions change, and differentiation is no longer possible in settings that are far from smooth. And so, on their flight back to Austria, Kunzinger and Sämann wondered whether they could devise alternative methods — ones that would still work in the inhospitable environments where the usual tools of calculus broke down.

Clemens Sämann has helped prove important singularity theorems in space-times that “could have corners, edges and folds.”
Der Knopfdrücker
The pair wouldn’t start working on the problem in earnest for another year. But since then, they’ve made significant advances toward their goal. They’ve found new ways to estimate curvature and other geometric properties without relying on smoothness and differentiation. In collaboration with other researchers, they’ve used their methods to rederive (and sometimes strengthen) core theorems about the universe without depending on Einstein’s equations, putting those theorems on even firmer mathematical footing.
And they’re now part of
an ambitious new program
— launched last year under the direction of
Roland Steinbauer
, another University of Vienna mathematician — that aims to provide “a new geometry for Einstein’s theory of relativity and beyond.”
“Standard general relativity talks about geometric objects, namely space-times, but only if they behave nicely enough,” Steinbauer said. “With this new framework, we can go beyond that. We can handle very edgy objects, very badly behaved objects.”
A Path Via Triangulation
When Kunzinger and Sämann started working together in 2016, their first goal was to revisit one of the most basic concepts to appear in Einstein’s equations: curvature.

data.title: Meta says it wont sign Europe AI agreement, calling it growth stunting overreach
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Meta Platforms拒绝签署欧盟的人工智能行为准则，称其过度监管将抑制增长。全球事务主管Joel Kaplan表示，该准则引入了多项法律不确定性，超出《人工智能法》的范围。该准则旨在帮助企业遵守去年通过的《人工智能法》，以提高技术透明度和安全性。此前，ASML Holding和Airbus等公司曾呼吁欧盟推迟实施该准则两年，而OpenAI已承诺签署。Kaplan强调，这一过度监管将限制前沿AI模型在欧洲的发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟AI法案及其自愿行为守则的有效性和影响

不同观点：
• ankit219：认为法案的性质不明确，40家欧盟公司要求推迟两年实施。提到法案中对模型提供者责任的规定对开源模型来说非常严格，并指出自愿签署行为守则可能减少审查压力。
• throwpoaster：担心欧盟会像对网站一样，对LLM模型增加弹出提示，对此表示不满。
• vanderZwan：承认自己有偏见，认为Meta的反应让人觉得AI协议是当前所需的，但其实对协议内容并不了解。

Meta Platforms
declined to sign the European Union's
artificial intelligence
code of practice because it is an overreach that will "stunt" companies, according to global affairs chief Joel Kaplan.
"Europe is heading down the wrong path on AI," Kaplan wrote in a post Friday on
LinkedIn
. "This code introduces a number of legal uncertainties for model developers, as well as measures which go far beyond the scope of the AI Act."
Last week, the
European Commission
, the executive body of the EU, published a final iteration of its code for general purpose AI models, leaving it up to companies to decide if they want to sign.
The rules, which go into effect next month, create a framework for complying with the AI Act passed by European lawmakers last year. It aims to improve transparency and safety surrounding the technology.

data.title: Ask HN: GCP Outage?
data.author: grilledchickenw
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Cloud及相关服务（如Firebase、Google登录、Google Workspace等）发生硬件故障及部分服务中断，用户反馈问题并讨论可能的影响和解决方案。

不同观点：
• blitzar表示系统宕机，选择暂时离开工作，表明对问题暂无解决方案。
• dondraper36和palcu引用官方状态页面，确认在us-east1区域存在硬件问题，提供具体事件链接，表明问题已被官方确认。
• Ironlink具体描述了在EU区域观察到的系统缓慢及500和503错误，持续约10分钟，表明问题不仅限于us-east1区域。
• abhisek提到在维护期间由于Kubernetes升级导致整个集群出问题，尽管状态页面显示正常，支持案例花了6小时才解决，质疑官方状态页面的准确性。
• freedomben提到早上遇到一些50x错误，认为虽然是部分中断，但可能预示更严重的问题，表现出对潜在更大问题的担忧。
• lebski88提到VPN重启引发了一些小问题，但认为这次事件比上一次好一些，提供了一些对比信息，表明问题影响程度不一。
• tosh指出Firebase Firestore在us-east1区域要么宕机要么延迟很高，进一步确认特定服务在特定区域的问题。
• ghxst报告公司内多人遇到问题，主要在美国，但随后更新称欧盟也出现问题，表明问题蔓延到其他区域。
• romanzubenko和staletofu提到谷歌登录和GCP登录问题，进一步扩展了问题的影响范围到身份验证服务。
• jeanlucas提到巴西用户遇到的单点登录（SSO）和Google Workspace工具加载问题，提供具体时间戳，表明问题具有全球性影响。
• ChrisArchitect提供另一个事件链接，进一步扩展讨论到Google Apps的状态。
• dangoodmanUT借此机会强调多云策略优于多区域策略，认为最近多次云服务中断（GCP和Cloudflare）暴露了单一云服务商的脆弱性，提出对云服务架构的反思。
• archiolidius提到YouTube API部分服务中断，扩展了受影响的服务范围。

补充讨论：
• 多个用户引用官方状态页面链接，表明问题已得到官方确认，但具体影响范围和持续时间仍在变化。
• 用户反馈表明问题不仅限于单一区域或服务，而是影响多个区域和多种Google服务，包括身份验证、API和分析工具等。
• dangoodmanUT的评论引发了对云服务架构的讨论，认为多云策略可以提高可用性，是对单一云服务商依赖的潜在解决方案。
• 争议的焦点在于官方状态页面的准确性和问题解决的速度，abhisek的评论质疑了状态页面的可靠性，并提到支持案例解决时间过长。

data.title: DuckDuckGo now lets you hide AI-generated images in search results
data.author: moose44
data.article_summary: 隐私浏览器DuckDuckGo推出新功能，允许用户在搜索结果中过滤掉AI生成的图片。用户可以在进行搜索后，进入图片标签页，通过新的“AI图片”下拉菜单选择显示或隐藏AI图片。该功能响应了用户反馈，帮助避免低质量的AI图片干扰搜索结果。过滤器基于手动整理的开源屏蔽列表，虽然不能100%过滤掉所有AI图片，但能显著减少其数量。DuckDuckGo计划未来添加更多过滤选项。这一功能推出之际，互联网正被大量低质量的AI内容淹没。

44606803.article_content:
Privacy-focused browser DuckDuckGo is
rolling out
a new setting that lets users filter out AI images in search results. The company says it’s launching the feature in response to feedback from users who said AI images can get in the way of finding what they’re looking for.
Users can access the new setting by conducting a search on DuckDuckGo and heading to the Images tab. From there, they will see a new dropdown menu titled “AI images.” Users can then choose whether or not they want to see AI content by selecting “show” or “hide.”
Users can also turn on the filter in their search settings by tapping the “Hide AI-Generated Images” option.
Image Credits:
DuckDuckGo
DuckDuckGo’s new feature comes as the
internet is being flooded
with AI “slop,” which refers to low-quality media content made using generative AI technology.
“The filter relies on manually curated open-source blocklists, including the ‘nuclear’ list, provided by uBlockOrigin and uBlacklist Huge AI Blocklist,” DuckDuckGo said in a
post on X
. “While it won’t catch 100% of AI-generated results, it will greatly reduce the number of AI-generated images you see.”
DuckDuckGo says it plans on adding additional filters in the future, but didn’t provide specifics.
It’s worth noting that DuckDuckGo’s example for the new feature depicts an image search for a baby peacock, likely in reference to Google facing
controversy last year
for showing more AI-generated images of baby peacocks rather than real-life images when conducting an image search for the bird.

data.author: DonnyV
data.article_summary: 文章指出，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能导致在x.com网站上出现问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序后重试，以解决潜在的故障。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过此方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：H1B签证政策及其对美国就业市场的影响

不同观点：
• **wippler** 认为图表具有误导性，因为每年新增H1B签证数量固定为85,000，增长的是续签人数，而非新批准人数。特别是由于绿卡积压，印度和中国籍H1B持有者不断续签，导致人数增加。他还提到签证持有者通常会转为永久居民，但由于国家配额限制，许多人无法如愿。

• **eitally** 质疑图表的意义，认为H1B签证的线性增长与科技行业的快速扩张不成比例。他提出，除非能证明新增就业岗位中移民占比过高，否则图表没有实际价值。

• **tboyd47** 支持引进顶尖人才，并建议允许H1B持有者创业和自由换工作，认为这样更有利于创新。

• **silisili** 主张在当前就业环境下暂停新的H1B签证申请，认为现状对美国本土求职者不公。

• **randomizedalgs** 提供谷歌员工数量在同一时期增长了五倍的视角，暗示软件行业增长可能超过H1B签证数量的增加。

• **lurker919** 提出图表是否混淆了新签证和续签签证数量的问题，指出由于绿卡积压，续签人数不会下降。

• **websap** 作为H1B持有者，表达了对当前美国就业环境的担忧，尤其是在反移民情绪高涨的背景下，并询问其他国家的移民和工作机会。

• **forinti** 认为H1B持有者占总人口和劳动力比例极小（分别不到0.2%和0.3%），暗示影响有限。

• **mikece** 质疑是否美国计算机科学毕业生真的不如H1B申请者，建议研究并解决这一问题，以保护本土求职者。

• **paxys** 和 **steveBK123** 对H1B增长与科技行业增长的对比表示疑问，认为需要更多数据支持。

data.title: ICE is getting unprecedented access to Medicaid data
data.author: josefresco
data.article_summary: 美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）获得了一项协议，允许其访问近8000万 Medicaid 用户的个人数据，以获取有关在美外国人的身份和位置信息。根据该协议，ICE 将能够访问包含敏感医疗信息的数据库，包括家庭住址、电话号码、社保号码等。尽管协议最初提到访问银行和IP地址信息，但后续条款仅限定为获取 Medicaid 受益者的性别、种族和族裔信息。该协议有效期为两个月，从7月15日至9月15日。此举是特朗普政府加强移民执法的举措之一，旨在加速驱逐移民。然而，前奥巴马政府时期的 ICE 负责人约翰·桑德韦格警告，这可能导致人们因担心被驱逐而不敢申请福利或就医。特朗普政府则声称，此举旨在防止 Medicaid 资金被非法使用，并确保福利发放给合法公民。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府机构（尤其是ICE）获取和使用数据的合法性、道德性以及潜在后果

不同观点：
• **权力滥用担忧**：duxup和donatj等用户认为，这是行政部门扩权的行为，ICE可以不受典型宪法保护的限制获取和使用数据。这种权力扩张被视为对公民权利的威胁，尤其是在ICE已有许多争议行动的背景下。
• **合法性辩论**：michael1999指出，根据HIPAA法律，执法部门可以在某些情况下无需 warrant（搜查令）即可获取健康数据，但这一规定被认为容易被滥用，且原本的保护措施在立法过程中被削弱。
• **广泛社会问题**：ktallett认为，政府机构不应获取私人数据，尤其是像ICE这样有争议的部门。同时提到移民问题只是美国社会众多问题中的一个，而非核心问题。
• **数据安全与集中化风险**：loourr和tastyfreeze强调了政府集中收集数据的风险，指出当政府已经拥有数据时，获取这些数据变得非常容易，不再需要法律程序如传票。
• **对特定人群的威胁**：diamond559和ck2认为，这一行动不仅是针对移民，未来可能会针对持不同政见者。ck2进一步提到，如果每天有7000人被逮捕，社会将迅速变得非常恐怖。
• **预算与政府扩张**：theyinwhy和jasonlotito指出，ICE的巨额预算（与五角大楼相同）以及保守派支持的大政府权力扩张令人担忧。这被视为与他们原本主张的小政府理念相悖。
• **技术与现实对比**：anthk提到，过去在游戏中看到的反乌托邦情节如今正在变成现实，反映出对当前社会趋势的忧虑。

补充讨论：
• **对具体政策误解的反驳**：kevingadd提到，获取 Medicaid 数据并不意味着非法移民能够绕过所有检查，因为该项目要求提供社会安全号码和公民身份信息。这表明部分讨论建立在对政策误解的基础上。
• **极端政治观点**：dandanua认为，美国正被一个“纳粹组织”控制，法律和普通人都不再被重视，反映出对当前政治体制的极端不信任。

争议焦点：
• **ICE获取数据的合法性与正当性**：一部分人认为这是合法的权力行使，另一部分人则认为这是对公民权利的严重侵犯，且容易被滥用。
• **政府数据集中化与隐私保护的平衡**：数据集中化带来的安全隐患和隐私侵犯风险成为讨论核心，尤其是当政府机构如ICE能够轻松获取这些数据时。

Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials are getting access to the personal data of nearly 80 million people on Medicaid in order to acquire "information concerning the identification and location of aliens in the United States,” according to an information exchange agreement viewed by WIRED.
The agreement, which is titled “Information Exchange Agreement Between the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for Disclosure of Identity and Location Information of Aliens,” was signed by CMS officials on Tuesday and first reported by
AP News
.
Per the agreement, ICE officials will get login credentials for a Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) database containing sensitive medical information, including detailed records about diagnoses and procedures. Language in the agreement says it will allow ICE to access personal information such as home addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, banking data, and social security numbers. (Later on in the agreement, what ICE is allowed to access is defined differently, specifying just “Medicaid recipients” and their sex, ethnicity, and race but forgoing any mention of IP or banking data.) The agreement is set to last two months. While the document is dated July 9, it is only effective starting when both parties sign it, which would indicate a 60-day span from July 15 to September 15.
The move comes as President Donald Trump’s administration has continued to expand its crackdown on immigration. The administration aims to deport
3,000 people per day—
four times as many
as were deported in the fiscal year of 2024, according to ICE. Its plans to do so seemingly involves vacuuming up data from across the government. WIRED previously reported that the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and DHS were working on a
master database
, pulling in data from across DHS and other agencies, in order to surveil and deport immigrants.
Medicaid, state and federally government-funded health care coverage for the country’s poorest, is largely
available only to some non-citizens
, including refugees and asylum seekers, survivors of human trafficking, and permanent residents. Some states, like New York, provide Medicaid coverage for children and pregnant people, regardless of their immigration status. States report their Medicaid expenditures and data to the federal government, which reimburses them for some of the costs.
“This was never even considered during my five years at DHS working on immigration enforcement,” says John Sandweg, the acting director of ICE during President Barack Obama’s administration. “You want to be careful of a possible chilling effect where people who might apply for benefits and be eligible for benefits—or who seek emergency medical care—won’t do so because they’re worried the information they provide at the hospital could make them a target for immigration action.”
This isn’t the concern of the administration now, spokespeople tell WIRED. “Under the leadership of Dr. [Mehmet] Oz, CMS is aggressively cracking down on states that may be misusing federal Medicaid funds to subsidize care for illegal immigrants,” Andrew Nixon, the director of communications at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), tells WIRED. “This oversight effort—supported by lawful interagency data sharing with DHS—is focused on identifying waste, fraud, and systemic abuse. We are not only protecting taxpayer dollars—we are restoring credibility to one of America’s most vital programs. The American people deserve accountability. HHS is delivering it.”
“President Trump consistently promised to protect Medicaid for eligible beneficiaries. To keep that promise after Joe Biden flooded our country with tens of millions of illegal aliens, CMS and DHS are exploring an initiative to ensure that illegal aliens are not receiving Medicaid benefits that are meant for law-abiding Americans,” says assistant secretary of DHS Tricia McLaughlin. (Biden did not allow “tens of millions” of immigrants into the US: even the Heritage Foundation, the conservative think tank behind
Project 2025
, claimed that
6.7 million people
entered the country illegally under Biden as of January 2024.)
The agreement states that its purpose is not to identify waste, fraud, and abuse or examine whether immigrants are receiving impermissible benefits, but to allow ICE to "retrieve information concerning the identity and location of aliens in the United States."
“It highlights to me that the targeting has moved well beyond criminal aliens, you don’t look at data like this unless you’re looking well beyond people convicted of crimes," says Sandweg.

data.title: Experts lay into Tesla safety in federal autopilot trial
data.author: duxup
data.article_summary:
本周，迈阿密联邦法院开始审理一起涉及特斯拉Autopilot系统的过失致死案件。这是联邦法院首次审理此类案件。过去，特斯拉Autopilot曾涉及多起致命车祸，包括2018年沃尔特·黄的死亡事件，其家属与特斯拉达成秘密和解。近日，特斯拉还就2019年杰里米·班纳的死亡案件达成和解。然而，在佛罗里达州2019年另一起致死车祸的联邦案件中，特斯拉未能与原告达成和解。这起事故中，乔治·麦吉驾驶的特斯拉闯过停车标志，撞死纳伊贝尔·贝纳维德斯并使迪伦·安古洛脑部受伤。

专家Missy Cummings作证称，特斯拉Autopilot存在缺陷，且特斯拉明知系统设计不足却放任使用。她指出，特斯拉对车祸数据统计不当，并误导安全声明。统计学家门德尔·辛格也批评特斯拉的数据处理方式。尽管特斯拉可能尝试和解，但原告似乎更关注寻求正义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉Autopilot系统的安全性和功能性，特别是在涉及自动驾驶机制和监管的情况下。

不同观点：
• [bryanlarsen] 认为特斯拉的Autopilot在2019年时主要是一个车道保持和交通感知巡航控制系统，并不能识别停止标志或红灯。他指出，此次审判的焦点是确保驾驶员在使用Autopilot时保持警觉的机制，而非自动驾驶功能本身。

• [edgineer] 持批评态度，认为特斯拉允许车辆在其设计不适合的条件下运行是“荒谬的”。他将此问题与汽车巡航控制功能进行对比，并提到2021年基础设施和就业法案中关于所有新车必须安装紧急熄火开关的规定，认为这是过度监管，同时希望新提出的“无熄火开关汽车法案”能有所进展。

• [abbotcabbot] 对事故场景中的具体情况提出疑问，认为描述中车辆经过停止标志并撞到行人涉及两个独立错误，因为停止标志和行人并没有直接关联，质疑事故是否因系统错误累积导致。

补充讨论：
• 关于Autopilot系统是否“欺骗性”命名以及其功能是否符合消费者预期的争论。
• 对政府监管（如紧急熄火开关法案）的看法，有人认为过度监管，有人认为必要。
• 对Autopilot机制中驾驶员警觉性保障的有效性存在争议，特别是事故场景下该机制是否失效。

争议焦点：特斯拉Autopilot系统的实际功能与消费者预期的差距，以及在何种条件下允许自动驾驶辅助系统运行是合理的。同时，关于政府监管措施是否适当也是讨论中的一个争议点。

This week, a federal court in Miami started hearing a wrongful death case involving Tesla's
crash-prone
Autopilot driver assistance system. It's not the first time that Tesla Autopilot has been implicated in fatal traffic crashes, but it is the first time that a federal court has heard such a case.
Until now, the most high-profile court case involving Tesla Autopilot was probably the California trial over the death of Walter Huang, who was killed in 2018 when his Tesla Model X steered itself into a concrete highway divider.
Huang's family took Tesla to court
in April 2024
but quickly settled with the automaker
under terms that have been kept secret.
And earlier this week,
Tesla settled another Autopilot lawsuit concerning the death of Jeremy Banner in 2019. In that case, the Tesla's sensors
failed to recognize a tractor-trailer crossing the highway
and collided with it, shearing the top off the car and killing Banner.
So far, Tesla has been unable to settle with the plaintiffs in the federal case, which also concerns a fatal crash in 2019 in Florida. In this case, in April 2019, a Tesla being driven by George McGee sped through a stop sign in the Florida Keys and struck Naibel Benavides and Dillon Angulo, who were standing near their car and stargazing. Benavides was killed, and Angulo was left with a brain injury.
"I feel like we were experimented on, and this technology was out on the road before it was safe,"
Angulo told an NBC interviewer
in 2023.
What did the experts say?
Missy Cummings, a former fighter pilot and expert on autonomous systems, pulled few punches. Cummings,
who received torrents of abuse
from Tesla fans after being appointed to a senior advisor position at the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in 2021, told the court that "it is my professional opinion that Tesla's Autopilot is defective because Tesla knowingly allows the car to be operated in operational domains for which it is explicitly not designed for."
Tesla's cockpit monitoring of drivers to ensure they remain alert "is simply not sufficient as keeping the driver engaged," Cummings told the court. And Tesla has a long history of "promoting the abuse and misuse of Autopilot." Cummings' testimony detailed her work at NHTSA investigating other fatal Tesla crashes, like the 2016 death of Joshua Brown, and detailed some of the interactions she and her agency had had with the car company.
For example, she said Tesla "clearly recognized that mode confusion is an issue—this is where people, for example, think the car is in Autopilot and don't understand that the Autopilot has disengaged," she told the court.
Cummings also referred to the deposition of Tesla autopilot firmware engineer Ajshay Phatak. Phatak's deposition told the court that the company did not keep good track of Autopilot crashes prior to 2018, and Cummings pointed out that "it was clear they knew that they had a big problem with people ignoring the warnings. Ignoring the hands-on requests. And...as you know, prior to this accident. It was known to Tesla that they were having problems with people ignoring their warnings."
Tesla's abuse of statistics to make misleading claims about safety is nothing new:
In 2017, Ars found out that Tesla's claim about Autopilot reducing crashes was not at all backed by data
, which, in fact, showed the driver assist increased crash rates.
Mendel Singer, a statistician at Case Western University School of Medicine, was very unimpressed with Tesla's approach to crash data statistics in his testimony. Singer noted that he was "not aware of any published study, any reports that are done independently... where [Tesla] actually had raw data and could validate it to see does it tend to make sense" and that the car company was not comparing like with like.
"Non-Teslas crashes are counted based on police reports, regardless of safety system deployment," Singer said. Further, Tesla kept misleading claims about safety on its website for years, Singer pointed out. When asked whether he would have accepted a paper for peer review from Tesla regarding its reports, "that would have been a really quick and easy rejection," he said.
While it's possible that Tesla will still settle this case, we may also see the trial carried out to its conclusion.

本周，迈阿密联邦法院开始审理一起涉及特斯拉Autopilot系统的过失致死案件。这是联邦法院首次审理此类案件。过去，特斯拉Autopilot曾涉及多起致命车祸，包括2018年沃尔特·黄的死亡事件，其家属与特斯拉达成秘密和解。近日，特斯拉还就2019年杰里米·班纳的死亡案件达成和解。然而，在佛罗里达州2019年另一起致死车祸的联邦案件中，特斯拉未能与原告达成和解。这起事故中，乔治·麦吉驾驶的特斯拉闯过停车标志，撞死纳伊贝尔·贝纳维德斯并使迪伦·安古洛脑部受伤。

专家Missy Cummings作证称，特斯拉Autopilot存在缺陷，且特斯拉明知系统设计不足却放任使用。她指出，特斯拉对车祸数据统计不当，并误导安全声明。统计学家门德尔·辛格也批评特斯拉的数据处理方式。尽管特斯拉可能尝试和解，但原告似乎更关注寻求正义。
44607547.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉Autopilot系统的安全性和功能性，特别是在涉及自动驾驶机制和监管的情况下。

不同观点：
• [bryanlarsen] 认为特斯拉的Autopilot在2019年时主要是一个车道保持和交通感知巡航控制系统，并不能识别停止标志或红灯。他指出，此次审判的焦点是确保驾驶员在使用Autopilot时保持警觉的机制，而非自动驾驶功能本身。

• [edgineer] 持批评态度，认为特斯拉允许车辆在其设计不适合的条件下运行是“荒谬的”。他将此问题与汽车巡航控制功能进行对比，并提到2021年基础设施和就业法案中关于所有新车必须安装紧急熄火开关的规定，认为这是过度监管，同时希望新提出的“无熄火开关汽车法案”能有所进展。

• [abbotcabbot] 对事故场景中的具体情况提出疑问，认为描述中车辆经过停止标志并撞到行人涉及两个独立错误，因为停止标志和行人并没有直接关联，质疑事故是否因系统错误累积导致。

补充讨论：
• 关于Autopilot系统是否“欺骗性”命名以及其功能是否符合消费者预期的争论。

• 对Autopilot机制中驾驶员警觉性保障的有效性存在争议，特别是事故场景下该机制是否失效。

争议焦点：特斯拉Autopilot系统的实际功能与消费者预期的差距，以及在何种条件下允许自动驾驶辅助系统运行是合理的。同时，关于政府监管措施是否适当也是讨论中的一个争议点。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Steam商店的页面加载问题及其背后的原因，包括数据使用量过大、用户连接速度慢以及对低带宽用户的影响。同时，部分用户讨论了Steam的用户界面变化及数字商品的实用性。

不同观点：
• Fogest认为Steam商店页面加载缓慢可能是因为页面加载了大量数据，导致其网络连接难以应对，并怀疑这可能是其ISP没有限制其他服务但限制Steam的原因。他计划监控网络流量以确认问题。

• ThatMedicIsASpy通过具体例子指出，Steam的某些页面（如积分商店）会加载20-30MB的数据，主要是GIF、WebM和动画PNG，这可能是导致页面加载缓慢的原因。

• LorenDB批评了一些ISP仅提供有限数据流量的做法，认为这在未来几年内是不够的，尤其是在使用数据密集型服务时。

• autoexec质疑数字贴纸的存在意义，认为数字商品没有明确的用途，与其他讨论点形成对比。

• msgodel分享了过去使用Steam的负面经历，指出Steam对数据的需求一直很大，并提到因为过去的糟糕体验，他现在更倾向于从GOG购买游戏。

• sitzkrieg认为像Steam这样转向基于Web的用户界面（UI）的程序在各方面都变得更差，过去的UI体验更好。

• micromacrofoot是Steam的忠实粉丝，但指出Steam由于其自由放任的开发方式可能正在失去优势，经常遇到商店的随机问题。

• ars指出大公司似乎不关心低带宽用户，分享了在低速网络下使用其他应用（如Teams和Outlook）的糟糕体验，并建议新程序员应使用旧电脑学习如何提高效率。

补充讨论：
• leshokunin以幽默的方式回应了sitzkrieg的评论，问道是否感到“欣喜”。

• dsizzle提到Substack应用也出现了类似的问题，与其他用户分享的体验相呼应。

• smittywerben提供了背景信息，指出Steam从未真正支持在移动设备上使用商店，认为这在一定程度上是合理的。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点之一是Steam页面加载缓慢的原因，一些人认为是用户网络连接问题，另一些人则认为是Steam页面数据量过大导致的。
• 数字商品（如贴纸）的实用性和意义也被质疑，与其他用户对Steam功能的讨论形成对比。

data.title: Replication of Quantum Factorisation Records with a VIC-20, an Abacus, and a Dog
data.author: teddyh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过使用1981年的VIC-20 8位家用电脑、算盘和一只狗来实现和超越当前量子因数分解记录的实现方法。作者希望此工作能够激励未来在量子因数分解记录上的进一步尝试。文章包含对原文的一些小修订，以更正打字错误、澄清因数分解中sqrt(n)的用法，并添加了电子邮件地址。本文属于攻击与密码分析类别，并以预印本形式发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算、因子分解、图表错误、对量子计算进展的评价以及相关竞赛的讨论。

不同观点：
• [cbm-vic-20] 通过使用校准过的参考狗Scribble进行实验，验证了因子分解15和21的过程。然而，实验并不简单，因为Scribble很乖，几乎不叫。

• [brontitall] 认为图3中存在错误，指出无符号变量m总是 >= 0，导致while循环不会终止。

• [rahimnathwani] 提供了之前讨论的链接，并引用了一篇文章，指出“量子计算进展不能单凭能因子分解的最大数来衡量”，并引用Dan Bernstein的观点，认为如果量子计算遇到物理障碍，世界可能会变得更好。

• [tomgag] 分享了自己对整个事件的看法，支持rahimnathwani的观点，并提供了相关链接，进一步讨论量子计算的进展不应以能因子分解的最大数来衡量。

• [spr-alex] 提到qdayprize.org上的搜索空间太小，不足以成为一个有意义的竞赛，且规则未明确如何判断“量子性”的有效性。

• [mycall] 简单表达了对讨论的喜爱。

• [OhMeadhbh] 对Peter Gutmann的参与表示幽默回应。

• [hagbard_c] 以幽默方式描述了自己在研究弦理论时的情景，用食物和动物肢体类比弦理论的维度，增加了讨论的趣味性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是量子计算进展的评价标准，部分评论者认为不能单凭因子分解能力来衡量。
• 另一个技术性问题是对图表中错误的指出和讨论，[brontitall] 指出了图3中的潜在错误。
• 对量子计算竞赛的有效性和规则也提出了质疑，特别是在如何判断量子性方面。

Replication of Quantum Factorisation Records with an 8-bit Home Computer, an Abacus, and a Dog
Peter Gutmann
, University of Auckland
Stephan Neuhaus
, Zurich University of Applied Sciences
Abstract
This paper presents implementations that match and, where possible, exceed current quantum factorisation records using a VIC-20 8-bit home computer from 1981, an abacus, and a dog.  We hope that this work will inspire future efforts to match any further quantum factorisation records, should they arise.

data.author: throw0101c
data.article_summary: 很遗憾您提到的相关内容目前无法提供。让我们换一个共同感兴趣的话题、继续聊聊吧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术对经济的影响，资本分配，技术投资的可持续性及其实际经济回报

不同观点：
• niemandhier认为铁路促进了资本的社会分配和长期财富增长，而AI则导致资本集中在富人手中，可能减少中产阶级的财富，进而影响经济。
• jonas21对AI投资占GDP的1.2%不以为然，认为相比历史上其他技术变革如阿波罗计划、铁路或疫情刺激计划，这个比例并不极端。
• oytis希望AI的炒作结束后，其能力可以被用于更有价值的领域，如药物发现。
• gazpacho建议新数据中心应强制使用可再生能源，认为这对大公司来说成本增加不大，且有助于推动可再生能源技术发展。
• jsnell质疑AI投资是否真的从其他行业转移了资金，并指出如果经济不是零和游戏，那么投资的乘数效应应该同时适用于所有领域。
• lucbocahut反驳了经济是零和游戏的观点，认为AI投资是因为预期的高回报，其价值可能远超铁路。
• ksec认为半导体技术仍有至少10年的发展空间，尽管增速放缓，但技术进步足以支撑到2035年，尽管AI需求可能更高。
• gitfan86指出自动化会移除部分经济活动，而不是扩大经济，例如曾经重要的行业如制钉业如今利润低且无社会地位。
• mikewarot期待FPGA的突破能大幅降低AI计算成本。
• gsky认为讨论中未提及机会成本。
• tptacek质疑是否可以简单地将Nvidia的Q1业绩乘以4来年度化。
• asdev认为当前有多个经济泡沫的迹象。
• siavosh想知道需要什么才能改变市场对AI未达预期的看法。
• datadrivenangel质疑当前AI资本支出是否包括常规数据中心，而非纯AI相关投资。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到经济是否为零和游戏，以及AI投资是否从其他领域转移资金，这显示了对资本分配影响的关注。
• 技术发展的可持续性及其实际经济回报是讨论的另一个焦点，尤其是对半导体技术和AI计算成本的未来展望。
• 对AI投资泡沫的担忧以及市场预期未达成的可能性也是争议点之一。
• 环境影响和技术发展方向（如可再生能源和FPGA的应用）是其他值得注意的讨论点。

larger than a dog house
knows, no one thinks what you spent on renovation makes sense, not even you. Most
spouses
wish
they could fire
someone
for cause over most renovations.
In that light,
this WSJ explainer
of the ongoing
Federal Reserve renovations
is useful reading as various administration officials
feign dismay
at someone
renovating a building
that hasn't been renovated in ... ever. Shocked, I am shocked to find renovations going on in here.
On Tuesday, T***p said he was surprised to learn about the costly building renovations, given his view that Powell is a boring and unintelligent person. “I think he’s a total stiff, but the one thing I didn’t see him [as] is a guy that needed a palace to live in,” he told reporters.
Say what you will about Powell's monetary policy, either that
wallpaper doesn't go
¹, or Powell does, apparently.
¹ Writer Oscar Wilde's final words may or may not have been: "This wallpaper and I are fighting a duel to the death. Either it goes or I do.”.
Rough Notes:
Honey, AI Capex Ate the Economy
How extreme is
AI datacenter spending
? It is to the point that even Chinese President
Xi Jinping
is  warning about it. With more than
250 datacenters
under construction in his country, this week he
cautioned
against the
spending rush
, threatening to intervene:
“When it comes to projects, there are a few things — artificial intelligence, computing power and new energy vehicles. Do all provinces in the country have to develop industries in these directions?"
The U.S., however, leads the
capex spending
way. One analyst recently speculated (via
Ed Conard

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了现代计算中矩阵乘法的重要性及其在人工智能和深度学习中的核心作用。尽管NVIDIA通过Tensor Cores等技术大幅提升了矩阵乘法的速度，但预编译的矩阵乘法内核缺乏灵活性。当前的主要瓶颈在于数据移动，而非计算本身。为了优化性能，需减少数据移动，并将多个内核或算法融合成单个内核。NVIDIA的CUTLASS提供了定制矩阵乘法内核的工具，但仅支持NVIDIA GPU，限制了可移植性。为此，作者开发了CubeCL和矩阵乘法内核引擎，能够为任何GPU甚至CPU生成优化内核。文章还介绍了现代GPU的架构和执行粒度，强调了同步和内存访问优化对高性能计算的重要性。

State-of-the-Art Multiplatform Matrix Multiplication Kernels
Fri, Jul 18, 2025
Louis Fortier-Dubois
Nathaniel Simard
Few algorithmic problems are as central to modern computing as matrix
multiplication. It is fundamental to AI, forming the basis of fully
connected layers used throughout neural networks. In transformer
architectures,
most of the computation
is spent performing matrix
multiplication. And since compute largely determines capability, faster
matrix multiplication algorithms directly translate into more powerful
models
[
1
]
.
NVIDIA probably deserves much of the credit for making matrix
multiplication fast. Their early focus on building GPUs for gaming
drove major improvements in general-purpose linear algebra. As deep
learning took over, they introduced Tensor Cores — specialized units
designed to accelerate matrix multiplication in AI models.
With hardware evolving to support these new workloads, accelerators
have become increasingly complex, and writing high-performance code
for them remains challenging. To ease this burden, hardware vendors
like NVIDIA, AMD and Intel provide off-the-shelf matrix multiplication
kernels, typically integrated into tensor libraries. However, the
quality and performance of these kernels vary. While NVIDIA’s
implementations, through libraries like cuBLAS
[
2
]
and cuDNN
[
3
]
, are highly optimized,
a key limitation remains: as precompiled binaries, they lack flexibility
and extensibility.
In modern AI workloads, the primary bottleneck is no longer
computation. It's data movement. Moving data from memory to registers
often costs more than performing the actual calculations. The best way
to optimize for this is quite obvious: minimize data movement. A
powerful way to achieve this is to fuse multiple kernels or algorithms
into a single kernel
[
4
]
. For
matrix multiplication, it means executing element-wise operations on
the values calculated
just before
writing them to global memory.
Pre-built matrix multiplication kernels don't support this kind of composition,
making custom kernel implementations necessary.
This is why NVIDIA created CUTLASS
[
5
]
: a set of C++ templates that help developers tailor
matrix-multiplication kernels to their needs. However, it remains very
intricate to use and, of course, only works on NVIDIA GPUs.
As a result, using CUTLASS to optimize a model often comes at the cost
of portability. But wouldn't it be better to optimize models across
platforms? That’s why we built CubeCL
[
6
]
, and on top of it, a matrix multiplication kernel engine
[
7
]
that searches for and generates optimized kernels for any GPU and even
CPUs.
Not Just an Algorithm
One of the main challenges with matrix multiplication is that the
input shapes strongly influence which algorithm performs best. As a
result, no single algorithm is optimal in all cases; different shapes
require different strategies.
To address this, we built an engine that actually makes it very easy
to create different algorithms that are totally configurable. At its
core is a multi-level matrix multiplication architecture that we'll
explore in this blog.
...Or, skip the theory and
jump straight to benchmarks
.
A Bit on the Hardware First
Before diving into the solution, let's briefly review the architecture
of modern GPUs. A GPU consists of multiple streaming multiprocessors
(SMs), each capable of independently executing parts of a program in
parallel. Each SM has a fixed set of resources shared across multiple
concurrent executions.
There are three main levels of execution granularity:
Unit
(
thread
in CUDA,
invocation
in Vulkan/Wgpu):
the smallest execution entity performing computations.
Plane
(
warp
in CUDA,
subgroup
in Vulkan/Wgpu): a
group of (typically 32) units executing in lockstep and able to share
data efficiently through registers.
Cube
(
thread block
in CUDA,
workgroup
in Vulkan/Wgpu):
a group of units that execute on the same SM, sharing memory and able
to synchronize.
Grasping the concept of planes can be challenging when first
programming GPUs, because it’s extremely implicit. One of the GPU's
parallel axes is actually more efficient when executed in sync, but
this is generally not reflected in the code. Units within the same
plane perform more efficiently when they execute the same instruction
simultaneously, whereas branching is more acceptable between different
planes. Additionally, data access is faster when each unit, in turn,
loads from consecutive addresses, allowing a single instruction to
fetch a contiguous block of memory. This is known as
coalesced memory access
and is central to most memory optimizations. As a result, many high-performance
computing kernels treat the plane—not the individual unit—as the smallest
computation primitive, in order to avoid branching and maximize performance.

data.title: Show HN: I built library management app for those who outgrew spreadsheets
data.author: hmkoyan
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了librari.io的Beta版功能，该平台帮助用户轻松管理家庭图书馆。用户可以组织、跟踪和发现书籍，拥有多座图书馆并获取全面的统计数据。平台提供一整套管理工具，包括详细的统计分析，以及自定义书籍、作者和出版商的元数据字段，方便用户更好地管理他们的藏书。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人图书管理工具的选择与比较

不同观点：
• bryanhogan推荐使用Obsidian，并提到其可以通过frontmatter属性管理书籍信息，且有方便的书籍搜索插件。他还提到Obsidian被用于其他类型的收藏管理。
• iFire质疑Obsidian与传统工具Calibre相比的优劣，特别是在实体书籍管理方面。
• mythmon_指出当前许多图书管理工具缺乏多用户支持，并描述了理想的多用户管理功能，如Plex的例子。
• 9dev介绍了自己的项目Colibri，并建议添加从开放数据源（如OpenLibrary）导入数据的功能，以提高元数据质量。
• pixelmonkey推荐使用libib.com，并分享了自己利用ChatGPT和Google Books API将实体书转换为数字书架的经验。
• f_allwein分享了一个简单的方法：拍摄书架照片，然后通过照片应用搜索书脊上的文字。
• unavoidable认为图书管理应用的主要问题不在于应用本身，而在于书籍的索引和管理过程。
• dosco189希望有一个应用可以通过拍摄书架照片自动生成书目。
• bhattisatish有超过500本书，希望有一个简单易用的图书管理平台，支持多用户、自动分类、借阅状态等功能，并强调了数据导入和导出的重要性。
• DerArzt对网站的移动端性能、定价、以及与本地托管工具的比较提出了疑问，并关注该工具的独特卖点。
• rorylaitila分享了自己利用OpenAI视觉模型快速录入书籍信息的经验，并建议增加书籍封面照片自动提取功能。
• a0-prw关注是否可以通过扫描ISBN添加书籍，认为手动添加过于耗时。
• bl4kers希望能够将数据保存到本地数据库，以便自己管理数据和备份。
• egonschiele赞赏应用的设计和暗黑模式，并提出了对定价结构和隐私政策的关注，同时请求批量导入书籍的功能。
• jrussino希望有一个简单的方法来扫描书籍并打印像图书馆使用的书脊标签，但发现现有工具大多不适合个人使用。

补充讨论：
• 多用户支持是许多用户关注的一个重要功能，特别是对于家庭共享的书籍管理。
• 自动提取书籍信息和批量导入功能被多次提及，显示了用户对简化录入过程的强烈需求。
• 用户对应用的定价、移动端性能和数据管理方式（本地 vs. 云端）有不同的偏好和期望。
• 一些用户分享了自己利用技术（如ChatGPT、OpenAI视觉模型）简化图书管理过程的实际案例和经验。

data.author: kristoff_it
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了异步（asynchrony）、并发（concurrency）和并行（parallelism）之间的区别，强调了异步并不等于并发。作者指出，常见的误解是将并发与并行混淆，而忽视了异步的重要性。文章通过保存文件和创建TCP服务器的两个例子说明：在异步任务中，任务的执行顺序可以不按序，但仍然正确；而在并发任务中，任务的执行必须重叠。作者提出了以下定义：

1. **异步**：任务可以不按顺序执行且仍然正确。
2. **并发**：系统能够同时推进多个任务，通过并行或任务切换实现。
3. **并行**：系统能够在物理层面上同时执行多个任务。

作者认为，区分异步和并发有助于避免库作者重复工作、改善用户体验，并避免死锁等问题。在Zig语言中，异步并不意味着并发，这使得库作者可以使用`io.async`而不强制用户放弃单线程阻塞I/O。

Loris Cro
